title: Direct Evidence for Robust Bulk Band Gap Across the Charge Density Wave Transition in TiSe2
authors: Turgut Yilmaz, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Muhammad Awais Fiaz, Zhenxian Liu, Jerzy T. Sadowski, Abdullah Al-Mahboob, Asish K. Kundu, Shawna M. Hollen, Boris Sinkovic, Elio Vescovo
abstract: The mechanism driving the charge density wave (CDW) transition in TiSe2 has been debated for decades, with proposals ranging from an excitonic insulator to a lattice-driven instability. A central question remains whether the transition involves an opening or enhancement of the bulk band gap. Using high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we directly track the temperature evolution of the bulk band edges across the CDW transition at TCDW = 200 K. Contrary to the expectation of a gap-opening transition, we find that the size of the fundamental band gap remains constant from the high-temperature normal phase down to 160 K. While the CDW induces clear band-folding signatures and spectral weight redistribution, the underlying band extrema are unperturbed. These results demonstrate that TiSe2 does not undergo a temperature-driven electronic gap opening. Instead, they support a scenario where the transition is governed by a lattice symmetry-breaking reconstruction that folds, but does not gap, the electronic structure of a pre-existing band insulator.
summary: This experimental study used ARPES to investigate the nature of the Charge Density Wave transition in TiSe2. Contrary to expectations of an electronic gap opening, the researchers found that the bulk band gap remains robustly constant across the transition temperature. This strongly suggests the CDW is driven by a lattice reconstruction that folds existing bands rather than creating a new electronic gap.
main_problem: The central question is whether the Charge Density Wave (CDW) transition in TiSe2 involves an electronic gap opening or if it is driven by lattice reconstruction.
main_result: The fundamental band gap size remains constant across the CDW transition temperature, indicating that the transition is governed by lattice symmetry breaking and band folding rather than a true electronic gap opening.
method: High-resolution Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to directly track the temperature evolution of the bulk band edges.
model_or_system: The study investigates TiSe2, a narrow-gap semiconductor known for its CDW transition at TCDW = 200 K. The analysis compares electronic structure measurements across the normal and CDW phases.
key_observables: Temperature evolution of the bulk band gap size; positions of conduction and valence band edges; spectral weight redistribution signatures (e.g., Folded Valence Band).
important_parameters: CDW transition temperature ($T_{	ext{CDW}} \approx 200	ext{ K}$); Temperature range studied ($300	ext{ K}$ down to $160	ext{ K}$); Gap magnitude ($\sim 85-100	ext{ meV}$).
main_assumptions: The authors assume that their simultaneous measurement of both band edges in single EDCs eliminates methodological uncertainties present in previous gap measurements.
figures_summary: Figures show ARPES intensity maps and Fermi surface contours remaining nearly identical across the CDW transition, while other figures plot the measured bulk gap magnitude showing invariance with temperature.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the scientific debate surrounding the CDW mechanism. It then presents high-resolution ARPES data tracking band edges across $T_{	ext{CDW}}$, demonstrating constant gap size despite clear evidence of lattice-induced band folding signatures.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, understanding how lattice instabilities (like CDWs) interact with electronic structure without necessarily opening a gap provides insights into symmetry breaking mechanisms relevant to correlated electron systems and charge ordering phenomena.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Crystal structure of TiSe2 in the normal phase (upper panel) and the three-dimensional Brillouin zone showing the high-symmetry points Γ, A, M, L, K, and H (lower panel). (b) In-plane 2a × 2a periodic lattice distortion in the CDW phase. (c) Brillouin zone of the normal phase (red hexagon) and the CDW superstructure (dashed black hexagons). (d) Schematic electronic band structure of the normal phase. (e) Electronic structure in the CDW phase between 160 K and TCDW. Blue lines connect panels (d) and (e) to indicate that the bulk band gap remains unchanged across TCDW.

FIG. 2. (a–c) ARPES intensity maps along the A-L cut at various temperatures. Above TCDW (250 K), a dispersive valence band (VB) and a broad conduction band (CB) are observed. Between TCDW and 160 K, a folded valence band (FVB) emerges at the L-point (marked with red dashed parabola) while the CB remains largely unchanged. (d) Corresponding Fermi-surface maps around the L-point. Elliptical contours persist, even across the TCDW and down to 160 K. (e) Momentum-distribution curves (MDCs) at the Fermi level (EF ) extracted at the L-point from panels (d). Red curves represent Gaussian ﬁts to the conduction-band spectral feature. The momentum position remains nearly unchanged across temperature.

FIG. 3. (a,b) ARPES intensity maps measured with 119 eV linear vertical (LV) and 95 eV circular left (CL) polarized light, sensitive to the folded valence band (FVB) and conduc- tion band near the L-point and along the Γ-M, respectively.

FIG. 4. (a,b) Energy-distribution curves (EDCs) at the L- and M-points obtained from Figure 3(a,b), respectively. Blue and red dashed lines mark the valence and conduction band, respectively. EDCs at room temperature are obtained with 119 eV and 95 eV linear vertical (LV) polarized lights. (c,d) Gap versus temperature plots obtained from (a,b), respec- tively. Peak positions are extracted from ﬁts to the spectra, given in Supplementary Information Figure S3. Error bars represent the standard deviation of the ﬁtted peak positions obtained from the EDC analysis.
